# Simplify a dense paragraph into plain English with Cohere today

> **In short:** Cohere's free playground can rewrite dense paragraphs into plain English — you paste the text, give a clear instruction, and read the simpler version. Free to start, but it can't replace reading important legal or medical documents yourself.

You know the feeling: you open a contract, a research paper, or a long email from a lawyer, and the first paragraph looks like a different language. This guide shows you how to use Cohere — an AI writing assistant — to turn that wall of words into something a curious 12-year-old could follow. No coding, no setup headaches. By the end, you'll have a small habit you can use on any tough text you meet.

## Before you start
- A free Cohere account — sign up with an email at Cohere's website.
- A web browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge — any recent one will work).
- One dense paragraph you'd like to simplify — copy it ready to paste. Budget 10–15 minutes total.

## Step 1 — Open the Cohere playground
Go to Cohere's website and sign in. After you log in, look for a section labeled **Playground** or **Try it now** — it's usually the most prominent button on the dashboard, the place Cohere takes you to test prompts (a prompt is just the instruction and text you give the AI). Click it. A new page opens with a large empty text box near the top and some settings on the side. If you can't find it, look for a sidebar menu on the left with words like **Chat**, **Playground**, or **Lab** — different Cohere accounts show slightly different navigation, so don't worry if yours is laid out a little differently.
💬 Example: click the **Playground** tile on the Cohere dashboard after signing in.
You'll know it worked when you see a tall empty box labeled something like "Prompt" or "Message" with a button such as **Send** or **Generate** below it.

## Step 2 — Check the model and settings
Before you type anything, glance at the settings area — usually on the right side or in a small panel above the text box. Look for a model selector; a model is just the specific AI "brain" Cohere uses, and it might say **Command**, **Command R+**, or another Cohere name. Leave it on the default unless you have a reason to change it; the default is fine for this task. Also look for a **temperature** slider if one is visible — temperature controls how creative the response is, with lower meaning more predictable and higher meaning more varied. For simplifying text, the default setting usually works well.
💬 Example: model left on "Command" (or whatever default appears), temperature left alone.
You'll know it worked when you don't see any red warnings on the screen and the text box is still empty and ready for your input.

## Step 3 — Paste your dense paragraph
Now click inside the empty prompt box and paste the paragraph you want simplified. Paste the whole thing — don't summarize it first, because Cohere needs to see exactly what to rewrite. If your paragraph is longer than what fits comfortably on screen, that's fine; just paste it as one block. The free tier usually accepts a full page of typical text in one go. Don't add any instructions yet — just the raw paragraph for now. If you accidentally paste it twice, delete one copy before moving on.
💬 Example: paste a paragraph from a software license, a journal abstract, or an email from your bank.
You'll know it worked when the text appears in the box, the cursor is at the end, and no error message pops up.

## Step 4 — Add a clear simplifying instruction
This is the most important step. Click right after the pasted paragraph (or above it in a separate instruction line) and add a clear, plain instruction telling Cohere exactly what you want. Keep it short and direct — something like "Rewrite this so a 12-year-old can understand it" works much better than a vague "make this better". The clearer your instruction, the closer the result will match what you actually want. If you'd rather keep the paragraph separate from the instruction, some Cohere layouts have a small instruction field at the top — use that if you see one.
💬 Example: add the sentence "Rewrite the paragraph above so a 12-year-old could understand it. Keep the same meaning." right after your pasted text.
You'll know it worked when both the paragraph and your instruction are visible in the prompt area, with the instruction clearly readable.

## Step 5 — Run the prompt
Click the **Send**, **Generate**, or **Run** button — the exact word varies, but the button sits near or under the prompt box and is usually highlighted in color. Wait a few seconds. Cohere's reply will appear in the same window, usually directly below your prompt. Read it slowly. The shorter, plainer version should be there, but it might still feel a bit stiff — that's normal, and we'll fix it in the next step. If nothing happens after about 15 seconds, try clicking the button once more; sometimes the first click doesn't register.
💬 Example: click the highlighted button below the text box and wait for the reply to stream in.
You'll know it worked when you see a paragraph of plain English appear below your original text, and that paragraph is noticeably shorter and easier to read than what you pasted.

## Step 6 — Refine until it sounds right
If the first reply is too stiff, too long, or doesn't quite match what you needed, type a short follow-up telling Cohere what to change. This is the fun part — you can ask for shorter sentences, simpler words, a friendly tone, a bullet list, or all of the above. Each follow-up is just a normal message in the same box. If the reply dropped important meaning from the original, paste the original back in and try a more precise instruction, like "Keep all the obligations and rights, but use plain words." Don't worry about using the "right" words — Cohere responds well to plain English.
💬 Example: type "Make it even simpler. Use shorter sentences." or "Turn it into three bullet points."
You'll know it worked when the final paragraph reads smoothly, matches the meaning of the original, and you could explain it to a friend in two minutes.

## Common mistakes
- **Pasting without any instruction.** If you just paste a paragraph and hit send, Cohere usually responds with a summary or analysis, not a rewrite. Always add a clear instruction telling it what to do.
- **Asking for too many things at once.** "Make it shorter, simpler, friendlier, in bullet points, and translate it" gives muddy results. One change per follow-up is much more reliable.
- **Trusting the rewrite on high-stakes text.** A simpler version of a contract is great for understanding, but it is NOT legally binding. For decisions involving real money, health, or legal rights, read the original carefully or talk to a professional.
- **Forgetting to check the meaning.** Rewrites can drop small but important details. Skim the side-by-side and make sure no key fact, date, or condition went missing from the plain-English version.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the next time you get a confusing email from your bank, insurance, or a government office, paste the dense part into Cohere and ask for a plain version. You'll understand it in one read instead of three.
- **For your business or work:** if you write for non-experts — newsletters, internal guides, customer help pages — run your draft through Cohere with "rewrite so a non-specialist understands" and compare the two. It catches jargon you stop noticing.
- **If you're just getting started:** the easiest first move is to copy any paragraph from today's news and run it through Steps 1–6 above. The habit builds the moment you see how much easier the rewrite is to read.

## Try it now
Find one paragraph you've been avoiding — maybe in an email, a Terms of Service page, or a Wikipedia introduction — and run it through Cohere using the six steps above. Five minutes from now, you'll have a version that actually makes sense.
